# Bug Catalog: special-site developer review route

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-09-30**  
**Scope:** `World` query/command-line review entry → normal world movement →
`_try_trigger_item_site()` → first special encounter.

## What this flow does

The developer review route puts a reviewer just outside one named special-site
radius after they start a new game. It skips the opening tutorial and points
the camera at the site, but it must not open the encounter itself: the reviewer
has to move into the normal world trigger. It exists because hidden sites have
no player-readable coordinates, so the ordinary world route cannot presently
give a reviewer a conclusive trigger result.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `?special_site=reef` | browser query | Starts a focused normal-world review at the `reef` special-site boundary. |
| `--special-site-playtest=reef` | command-line argument | Same review entry for automated verification. |
| `_try_trigger_item_site(active_diver)` | world behavior | Starts the special encounter only after proximity is crossed with encounters enabled. |

## IO boundaries

- Browser query / command-line user arguments select the route.
- Scene tree starts the new-game world and creates the real battle node.
- No save writes beyond the existing New Game initialization; the route must
  not grant the reward merely for opening it.
- Physics time advances movement and proximity detection.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug (one sentence, failure mode) | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The review route directly dispatches a special battle, so it cannot prove the normal proximity trigger. | High — a false green review can ship a broken route. | Existing `?special=1` intentionally does exactly this. | captured contract | open |
| 2 | The review route leaves tutorial/onboarding pause active or starts inside the radius, so a reviewer cannot perform the intended one-step test. | High — the review link appears broken or auto-passes. | New Game, tutorial skip, and popups each own pause state. | decision/invariant | open |
| 3 | A review route silently disables encounters or does not point the player toward the target. | Medium — a correct engine trigger is reported broken. | The normal R toggle gates special sites and the game does not expose coordinates. | captured contract | open |
| 4 | A mistyped public review-site id skips normal onboarding but cannot stage a playable destination. | Medium — a shared review link becomes a dead end. | Query strings are user-editable and site ids are internal names. | decision/invariant | open |

## Test plan

### Bug #1 — direct-dispatch false positive

- **Test type:** captured contract.
- **Description string:**
  > `special-site review: remains in free world outside reef until movement crosses the real radius — guards against direct-dispatch false positives`
- **What it catches:** a future route that calls `_offer_special_encounter()` at setup or starts inside the trigger radius.
- **Self-critique:** It asserts battle absence before movement and real special
  battle presence after crossing. It does not depend on helper names or scene
  construction details, so a behavior-preserving refactor passes.

### Bug #2 — paused/unusable review entry

- **Test type:** decision/invariant.
- **Description string:**
  > `special-site review: skips tutorial/onboarding pause and preserves enabled encounters — guards against an unusable review link`
- **What it catches:** an entry that strands the reviewer in intro/UI pause or
  inherits a disabled encounter state, or writes a player save while reviewing.
- **Self-critique:** It observes world state needed for actual movement, not a
  specific popup implementation. A visual copy change does not affect it.

## Skipped

- Browser input/camera rendering — this needs the hosted Web export and a
  human reviewer; a headless scene test cannot prove it.
- General player discovery of special sites — explicitly an unresolved design
  defect, not behavior this developer route should hide.
- Every site id — `reef` is the focused review contract; site-table integrity
  belongs to the existing `verify/sites.gd` coverage.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught:** The focused route test caught no regression in this change;
  it passed with the route outside the real radius, free movement enabled, and
  a real special battle only after the boundary was crossed. The pre-existing
  special-encounter suite also passed.
- **Bugs characterized:** The production path was already sound when
  encounters were on: the failure reported in the review is discoverability,
  because the site is neither visibly marked nor reachable by human-readable
  directions. The new route proves the proximity behavior without disguising
  it as a direct `?special=1` dispatcher test.
- **Browser confirmation:** The exported focused URL showed the reviewer at
  the boundary with the one-step instruction visible. Holding forward long
  enough to cross it entered the Angler special battle; no query-string
  dispatcher or synthetic teleport was used in that browser check.
- **Bugs discovered during writing:** A raw headless script does not know the
  project's global classes until Godot has run one editor/import scan. The
  verification procedure now performs that scan first. A second potential bug
  was addressed in production code: an unknown `special_site` id now falls
  back to the ordinary game rather than skipping onboarding into an invalid
  review route.
- **Tests removed:** none.
